utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning to all. May we have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: For the Office of the Prosecutor, Gerard Dobbyn with Joanna Korner, and assisting us today as Case Manager is Jasmina Bosnjakovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic, Eugene O'Sullivan and Ms. Paula Lynch appearing for Stanisic Defence today. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. For Zupljanin Defence, Igor Pantelic and Dragan Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Would the usher please escort the witness back to the stand.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, while that's happening I'm not seeking to delay matters now, but I do want to raise the question with you, and this is a joint application by the Defence and Prosecution about the procedures of the admission of documents particularly in light of Your Honours ruling yesterday in respect to the Sanski Most documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: You are alerting us that you are going to deal with that at some point or you are going to do it now?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, as Your Honours asked for the witness to come in, I thought I'll leave it to a later stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Ms. Hanson.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Hanson, we discussed yesterday how your report came to be written. At one point you said you had prepared a memo for the Prosecution team in the Krajisnik case. Do you you remember?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If I understand that well, that means you worked as part of the Prosecution team in the Krajisnik case?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And if I understood this right, when you submitted to them this memo on Crisis Staff, they liked it and so they decided to instruct you to write a report and represent that report as an expert; right?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sure that when they were giving you these instructions, they suggested what form the report should take and what particularly to focus on; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as form, it was mostly a question of the formal presentation such as footnotes versus endnotes. I don't recall much input on the topics to focus on. At that point, I think they thought I had satisfied with the topics I had covered, but there was certainly some discussion of what it takes to change a memo to an expert report, more footnotes, footnotes in a certain form, table of contents, that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You also told us yesterday, I think on page 4044, that you drew the attention of your Prosecution colleagues to documents that do not support their case. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's part of my job. I do it all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you identify those documents, please, which do not support the Prosecution's theory of the case in your report?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I note in my report the differences in the pattern but -- trying to recall if I found documents specifically from Crisis Staffs because I review many different documents as a member the team.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Hanson, if you say that there are documents that do not support the Prosecution case and that you drew the Prosecutor's attention to them when you were writing this expert report, I'm asking you, can you tell me which are these documents reflected in your report. Can you specify them?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are not in my report, but I brought them to the attention of the Prosecution team.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So those documents that do not support the Prosecution case are not reflected in the report. You did draw the attention of the Prosecution to them but you did not include them in your expert report. Don't you think that it is the duty of the expert in keeping with the rules of this court to assist the Court in gaining knowledge of facts that they are not aware of in an objective manner?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I feel that it is very much the duty of the expert to assist the Court by presenting facts in an objective manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: How, then, do you imagine facts can be presented in an objective manner if the facts that do not support the Prosecution case did not find a place in your report? How does that make your report objective?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not find any documents that significantly changed the understanding of -- my understanding of the pattern of evidence as explained in my report. As I say, in the course of my review documents, I know it is one of my duties to bring to the attention of the Prosecution documents that appear potentially Rule 68. I'm not a lawyer, it's not my job to decide whether a document is or is not Rule 68, but I did not find anything significant enough to change my understanding of the documents I use.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me that ultimately it is the Trial Chamber that decides on the significance of these documents; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: My understanding is the Trial Chamber can only decide on the documents presented to it. My job is to -- part of my job is to assist the Prosecution team with identifying documents that should possibly be disclosed as Rule 68.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The key issue is precisely this one, since it is the Trial Chamber that decides on the basis of the evidence led here, do you believe it is not your duty to present to the Trial Chamber all the documentation, including the documents that do not support the Prosecution case? In other words, do you believe it is sufficient for you to have informed the Prosecutor that some documents are potentially 68? That is the only issue. What is your position?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot possibly present to the Court all the documentation even relevant to Crisis Staffs. It's my job as an expert to make a selection. It's my job as an expert to look at the -- all the documentation to determine a pattern, and if there was a consistent pattern that one area of my conclusions was quite wrong on the basis of documents that contradict it, of course I take it out -- I would rewrite my report, take it out of it. I found no such consistent body of evidence which contradicted what I wrote. On the contrary, looking at tens of thousands of documents of which thousands came from Crisis Staffs, I made a selection that I thought best represented the pattern I saw in the evidence. I would -- I've based my report on the evidence I found, so it's not that I started with conclusions and looked -- presented only those documents which supported them. Quite the opposite.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]. [Interpretation] We will now go through certain documents that I believe you did consider but for some reason they did not find their way into your report.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do we have the translation now? [Interpretation] Should I repeat?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Hanson, thank you for this clarification. I will now try to present to you certain documents that I believe you had access to, but for some reason, they did not find their way into your report, although I believe they have a considerable effect on the veracity of the claims in your report. I asked you yesterday whether you had shown your colleagues from the Prosecution the context in which the instructions of the 19th December 1991 were issued. That's P69. Do you remember this question?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember the question. Part of my job as an analyst in the leadership research team is to explain historical context to the Prosecution team and I did often. My specific tasking on Crisis Staffs was to present a report on the formation and operation of Bosnian Serb Crisis Staffs. But in other forms of my work, I do explain the historical context.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Would you agree with me -- and I would appreciate brief answers such as yes or no. I'll read out to you a couple of facts and events which I believe to be important to the context in which these instructions were given. Do you believe it's important, in terms of the context, that on the 19th December, the non-constitutional declaration of sovereignty adopted by the Assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina had a role to play?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, if I may, before you go into the details of documents, there is -- Ms. Hanson, is there procedurally or administratively a means of isolating your work as an expert from your ordinary work in the Office of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Once my report was identified as -- to be an expert report, then certainly in this case I was -- very concrete steps were taken that I not be part of team meetings, I not receive any team discussions on the case. I would receive specific questions to answer, but I was not told why -- how they would pertain to the case, once I was identified as an expert.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the light of the Judge's question, let me ask you one more thing. You said your first report was created on the basis of a memorandum written by you as part of the Prosecution team in Krajisnik, and then the Prosecutor's leading that case asked you to write it in the form of a report, and that is your basic report, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And then this basic report from Krajisnik was amended, adjusted, updated for the requirements of this case, and then finally, the last -- the latest version was made for the Karadzic case; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: After I -- my expert report was completed for Krajisnik, I continued to update it according to materials, documents, that came to my knowledge. I was not -- this was an ongoing project and I was not yet identified as -- I had not yet been informed by Stanisic/Zupljanin team that they would want my report for an expert witness, but it was simply one of my taskings, ongoing taskings to keep my report updated. So it was -- that was a matter of a couple of years, and then when the Stanisic/Zupljanin team said they wanted to use my report, then I had a more definite goal in the writing it, but it was an ongoing project updating it. And then yes, there is another version which I have further updated for Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, isn't it true that you drafted one report for the Stanisic case and then subsequently updated it in April 2008?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I say, this report for this case was based on my ongoing revision and updating of the report as written for Krajisnik. So I don't quite understand --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let me explain. In 2006 or 2007, you drafted a report on Crisis Staffs for the needs of the Mico Stanisic case. That was the first version. The version we are discussing now is the version of 15 February 2008. That's just over a year ago.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that this version here is essentially what I drafted in, I believe, February 2008. I -- at this point, I do not recall whether there was a version in 2006 or 2007. As I say, the Krajisnik report, I think, I originally wrote in 2002 and kept reworking it. I don't remember -- I don't recall giving -- drafting one in 2006 or 2007 for the Stanisic Prosecution team.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: To conclude whether you remember or not, are you saying to us that there were no instructions and no suggestions made by the Stanisic/Zupljanin Prosecution team in the sense of direction that you should take in writing your report?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was -- received some oral instructions that it would be logical to expand the police section because it was very brief in the original report, and I was given a list of the municipalities in the indictment with an indication that it would be preferable to draw my examples from those municipalities where possible. I did not receive a written set of taskings as I did in the Karadzic case, but this was from conversations mostly with the former Prosecutor, Anna Richterova.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You mean Richterova; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So if I understood this correctly, you did not receive written instructions but you received verbal instructions, and on that basis, you adjusted your report?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of the oral discussions and suggestions, I looked at the police, the issue of the police in more depth, looked at some more police documents, and of the examples which I already had in my footnotes, I gave more emphasis in the text to those examples from the indictment municipalities. I did not change my conclusions or my assertions in any fundamental way. It was simply the main change was better organisation, but that I had already been working on myself and a little more attention to the police section.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Isn't it true, madam, that essentially the conclusions you made in the Krajisnik case, you just expanded to include the police by interpreting the documents related to the police, including the Law on the Interior, in keeping with the conclusions you had already made?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The conclusions I had already made were based on the documents. I looked at the documents one more time and wrote my conclusions. But I certainly did not look at the documents in the light of proving pre-existing conclusions. I always draw my conclusions from the documentary evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's go back to the context of the document P69.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we can call it up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Hanson, we were discussing the context of events which led to this document on the 19th of December. I asked you whether you believed that in the context of these instructions, the adoption of the unconstitutional proclamation of sovereignty on the 15th of October by the Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina is significant, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer that question because I do not -- I'm not in a position to judge the constitutionality or not of it. As I understand, it was not a direct proclamation [Realtime transcript read in error "Prokuplje lamb maigs"] of sovereignty but a memorandum on sovereignty, and it occurred two months before the issuance of this document. However, it was one of the events and the interpretation of that memorandum of sovereignty was one of the events which was, yes, part of the lead-up to the conflict, part of the problems facing or the issues facing Bosnia at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your view, did the signing of the plan on the peaceful solution of the Yugoslav crisis on the 25th of November, 1991, under the leadership of Lord Carrington also have an impact on the context?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was certainly part of the general political context at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that on the 9th of December, 1991, the conference on Yugoslavia continued precisely here in The Hague --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I do apologise to interrupt my learned friend. It is a problem with transcript. This is page 10, line 9, the wording is: "As I understand, it not a direct Prokuplje lamb maigs of sovereignty..." It doesn't make sense to me so let's clarify that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I think Mrs. Hanson, you actually said it was not a direct --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I think that in LiveNote it came out correctly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. It's line 7, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Oh yes. Sorry, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Although maybe the topic is different.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Would you like me to clarify this, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Proclamation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. You said it was not a direct proclamation, it was a declaration on sovereignty, memorandum?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: A memorandum. But the word in question here is "proclamation."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So the question I was trying to ask before this was: Do you know that on the 9th December 1991, the conference on Yugoslavia continued precisely here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that exact date, but, yes, I certainly know that at this time of year, in that month, it was ongoing.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the statement made by the German government on the 14th of December, 1991, wherein they say, despite the warning of the UN Secretary-General Perez de Cuellar at the time, that they would not give up on the recognition of sovereignty of Slovenia and Croatia, which practically undermined the efforts of the conference here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware of that particular statement. I am aware of the general policy of the German government at the time. Whether that necessarily undermined peace efforts, I'm not -- I can't answer or I would not agree that it necessarily meant all peace efforts were -- would be undone.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, you know that on the 17th of December, 1991, the council of ministers of the European Union adopted a new declaration on Yugoslavia and decided on that occasion that they would recognise the independence of all Yugoslav Republics that accept the declaration on the criteria of recognition for all new states in Europe and the former USSR, with a proviso that the application be made until 23rd December 1991, and the promised date of recognition was the 15th of January, 1992. Are you aware of this? Are you aware of this decision of the council of ministers?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am aware in general terms, not of the specific dates and dead-lines, nor the specific terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware, since you are a trained historian, that on the same day, the 17th December, when this declaration was made by the council of ministers, President Izetbegovic declared that Bosnia-Herzegovina would definitely apply for recognition of its independence?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I'm not aware of the exact date but I am aware of his statement to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina, as the highest body, indeed, despite the opposition of co-presidents from the Serbian people really made that decision on the 20th December 1991, and the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina formally applied for recognition of its independence. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once again, I'm not sure of the specific dates, but that generally accords with my knowledge, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that this decision of the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina to formally apply for recognition of its independence was adopted by simple majority, 12 ministers for, and 8 against?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of the procedural details of this decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And the last thing I believe to be important for the context of the instruction that we are discussing is the fact that on the 23rd December 1991, the German government really and unilaterally, without waiting for other states of the European Union, recognised the independence of Slovenia and Croatia. And again, this is a curiosity, this came three weeks before the Vatican recognised the independence of these republics. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I don't know the specific date. I am aware that about that time the German government unilaterally recognised Slovenia and Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did you draw the attention of your colleagues from the Prosecution to this context and the events surrounding the adoption of these instructions of 19 December, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: As part of the leadership research team, it's our job to make sure that the Prosecution is aware of the historical context. I'm not -- the international negotiations were not part of my particular area of expertise, but other members of my team certainly made the Prosecution team aware.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Then let me ask you more specifically, you are a historian, a political analyst, you made this report, you say you have enough knowledge to provide an expert report on Crisis Staffs, you claim that this document on Variants A and B is a fundamental document. And tell me, in your view was the adoption of these instructions influenced by all these facts that we've just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's conceivable, but the only larger historical context that this document refers to is the Bosnian Serb plebiscite in November. But obviously the production of any document is going to be influenced by the historical context in which it's produced.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But don't you think that it is precisely these facts and this historical context were the key and basic reason for the adoption of these instructions?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The question that concerned me was not so much the reason for the adoption, but the consequences of the adoption of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, you know, Ms. Hanson, when a document is issued, it is necessary to know the intent behind it, and you are telling us that you established the intent based on the consequences, not the intent per se? Please answer briefly, yes or no. There's no need to go into any deeper explanation.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when the question has two parts and I agree with one but not the other, I have to -- I can't answer simply yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Then go ahead.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is necessary to know the intent behind a document if you are analysing it. In this case, I was asked to look at the formation of Crisis Staffs, not the historical context of this one document. I traced the formation of Bosnian Serb Crisis Staffs to this document. That's why it's in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But if a document came into being, you must know in which historical context and why it came to be. You cannot establish the reasons for the production of a document based on the consequences that followed, or am I wrong?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are not wrong. I agree, you have to know the context, but that doesn't mean that you put all of it in the report on the formation and operation of Crisis Staffs.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So if I understand this well, on one hand, your report is limited to the consequences that these Crisis Staffs produced in your opinion; on another hand, it's limited insofar as there are documents you did not include in the report, and it is also limited because you did not present the real historical context that led to the production of a key document for this report; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: My document -- my report is limited to my tasking which is to explain the formation and functioning of Bosnian Serb Crisis Staffs. To that end, I included all documents which I thought most representative, most helpful, and I did not try to introduce the entire context of Bosnia in late 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me, Mrs. Hanson, to cut a long story short, that history is very important for understanding the conclusions and certain documents. When I say history, I mean the historical context in which things are happening or documents are produced.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let us look at this document. You claim, if I understand your report correctly, as well as the assertions you made in your testimony in other cases, you claim that this is a fundamental document prescribing the pattern according to which Crisis Staffs of the Serbian Democratic Party were established in the whole territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina in December 1991; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I make clear in my report, they were not established everywhere in December 1991, but, yes, I do see this document as the founding document for the Bosnian Serb Crisis Staffs of December 1991 and early 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Hanson, it seems to follow from paragraph 19 in your report that you believe that this document is a binding instruction followed by Municipal Boards of the SDS? It's the first page of your paragraph 19.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that those who received the instructions regarded it as binding upon them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any reason to believe, then, that some Municipal Boards of the SDS did not receive these instructions? Did I understand that correctly?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm unable to draw conclusions as to just how many did or did not receive them. I know that they were received in many municipalities. I am restricted obviously to the documentary evidence which shows which ones did. There's not documentary evidence saying we didn't get these instructions. As I indicate in my report, not all municipalities did form Crisis Staffs in December 1991. Some were quite later. Whether that was because they hadn't received the instructions or did not regard them as applicable to their situation, I can't tell.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But you claim, if I understood you correctly, that all Municipal Boards of the SDS formed Crisis Staffs?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, my sentence reads that SDS Municipal Boards received instructions and formed Crisis Staffs. I cannot claim, nor do I, that they all did. In fact, I make it clear in my report that some apparently is it not until as late as March.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Madam, I'm not asking you about the time when they set them up, whether it was January, February, or March. I'm asking you: Is your claim that all Municipal Boards of the SDS whenever, never mind when, from January to March, did set up such Crisis Staffs?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not claim that because there are many municipalities that did I not look at for which we have no documentary evidence. There are many municipalities which were not directly affected by the war or contested territory and for which I have no evidence, so I can't claim that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, the territories that were not affected by the war and were not in contested areas, did not implement these instructions to form Crisis Staffs; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know because I'm limited to the documentary evidence in the possession of the OTP, and if the municipality was not one which was a focus of document collection, I can't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Wait a moment. Are you telling us that as a Prosecution expert, you were looking only at the municipalities from the indictment or you were trying to establish whether there was a general approach to these instructions in the whole territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was looking for a general approach to the entire territory. However, my research is necessarily limited to the documents in the possession of the OTP. Therefore, I cannot claim with any certainty about what happened in municipalities for which I have not seen documentary evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, you did not see any documents because it was your choice not to look at them not because they are not accessible in the Prosecution archives?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I looked -- I searched for all potentially relevant documents in the possession of the OTP. I did not discard any municipalities which were not in the indictment simply because they were not in the indictment. I used what I had available to me and, yes, I did do extensive searches for several years on everything available.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Madam, I have to admit that I'm confused by your answers. On the one hand, you are very clear, only to turn around and then in your attempt to clarify it and explain it, you actually go in a completely different direction, but because I don't really have too much time, I won't dwell on this any longer. Will you please take a look at the preamble of this document, P69, items 1 and 2 of the instructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's on page 2 in the e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Isn't it correct that items 1 and 2 actually describe the context and the intent of the Serbian Democratic Party and explains the reasons why these instructions are actually produced, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Since you had occasion to analyse this, you can agree with me, can't you, that when we analyse the language and the terminology used in this document, specifically on pages 2 and 4 in e-court, that's chapter 2, items 1 through 11, you will see that these terms for the most part relate to, or rather, point to this being a preparatory document. For instance, items 2, 5, 7, 9, and 11; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first degree is the preparatory degree, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The same is true of Variant B first level. For reference purposes these are items 2, 5, 8, 9 and 10; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If I understood it correctly, and I'm sure that you've had occasion to read through this document more times than I did, in fact the binding character of these preparatory instructions applies only to the instructions to establish the SDS Crisis Staff and to establish the Assembly of the Serbian People in the territory of certain municipalities; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't see that qualification in the first degree. Another element that they describe is the 24-hour duty watches, which we do see introduced in many places along with the Crisis Staff and the formation of the Serbian Assembly. So I see all the steps of the first degree as being regarded as binding by those who received this. I don't see that much distinction between or anything in the text or in the interpretation of the text as in the documents that they separated those -- those instructions from the rest of level 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Obviously there was a misunderstanding due to the interpretation. But you can agree with me, can't you, that for the most part, all the instructions for the first level actually relate to preparatory steps; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In the -- at the second level, the only thing that is binding, in fact, is - just bear with me for a moment, please - is the establishment of Crisis Staffs and of the Assembly -- the Municipal Assembly; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The formation of the Crisis Staff and the Assembly are part of the first degree.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right. In any case, it is your position that this document and everything that was done in connection with this document was actually produced in strict confidentiality; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm trying to recall. I know it was made public. The declarations of Serb Assemblies, Serbian Municipal Assemblies may not have been done secretly. It depended, I think, on the municipality. So I can't say that there was complete confidentiality on all moves. At that -- again, it's a question of the time-period you're talking about. In December, more likely to be confidential; by March, more likely to be open. It is certainly clear in the document that they intended this to be confidential, that there would be secret instructions given to the -- for the next level. And the front page says, you know, strictly confidential.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Madam, I am not going to quote your work but there are at least 15 occasions where you say this was done in strict confidentiality, and then in one place you say that this was not done publicly. So tell me this, and I am very clear, is it your position that these instructions and what was done pursuant to those instructions was done in secrecy in the course of January 1992, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: These instructions were secret. As I said, it may be that some of the declarations of Serb Municipal Assemblies were not secret, but on the whole it was regarded as secret. The instructions were regarded as confidential. The actions were not made public, to the best of my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Are you trying to tell me that an Assembly, a Municipal Assembly, an Assembly of a Serbian municipality was established in secret? Is that your claim?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I'm limited to the documents in my possession. These documents indicate that Assemblies were held and declared. How widely -- widespread they were announced depended on the municipality to municipality; but they were not, as far as I know, announced that they were made on the basis -- not publicly announced that they were made on the basis of the instructions. So the instructions were kept secret, but a Municipal Assembly could be declared, without reference to the secret instructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Madam, it is quite clear to me, and you don't have to repeat this, you have used a certain number of documents that you had at your disposal, and that's quite clear. And whenever I put the question to you, I too only referred to those documents that you actually had access to. And I'm asking you again now: Was there a single case where you can claim that the Municipal Assembly was actually established in secrecy? Can you remember or recall any such specific instance, yes or no? If you cannot, just say "I can't remember."

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have seen the documents declaring the formation of the Assembly. I cannot see from the documents themselves how widely disseminated this announcement was, so I cannot draw the conclusion on how public it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please show the witness P437.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That's under tab 4 in your binder. Yesterday you commented on this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P437, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: These are the minutes, or rather, the decision on the establishment of the Serb municipality of Zvornik. Do you recall discussing this document yesterday with my learned friend?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And I believe that you read out the preamble of this document where, among other, it says pursuant to Article so and so of the constitution and then decisions on territories of municipalities, and Article 4 of the instructions regarding the organisation and actions of the bodies of the Serb people in BH in a state of emergency of December 1991, the Municipal Assembly of Zvornik at its session of so and so adopted the following decision. Can you see here that they are actually referring here to what you call the secret instructions? Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In item 2, we see the areas of the existing municipality of Zvornik are to be considered the Serb municipality of Zvornik; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's certain areas, not the entire municipality. Certain areas are separating themselves from the current municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And that is also stated in item 3, it says, local communes and inhabited places and parts of the town local communes mentioned in Article 2 of this decision are being parted from the inclusion in the municipality of Zvornik. That's what is stated in item 3; correct? So tell me, please, towards the end, the very end, in Article 9 of this decision, right above the signature. That's on page 4 in e-court. I apologise. Very well, thank you. Can you see there under 9 it says: "This decision shall come into effect on the 8th day from the day of its publication in the bulletin of the Serbian people Javnost and in the bulletin of the Serbian municipality of Zvornik." In other words, not only was this decision on the establishment of the Serbian municipality of Zvornik absolutely public, but also since the instructions are mentioned in preamble and referred to, it's obvious that these instructions too were completely out in the open, that they were public; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not your sure when the bulletin of the Serbian municipality of Zvornik came out. I wanted to raise that earlier because I believe it was not published until later in the spring, but certainly if it was published in Javnost, yes, that's public, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, madam, if a decision on the establishment of an Assembly is to come into effect and it's to come into effect on the 8th day of its publication. That's what is stated there. In other words, it has to be made public so that it can come into effect. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Would you now please comment briefly for the benefit of the Trial Chamber the concept of Variant A and Variant B. In other words, I will put it to you and I hope that you will agree with me. Variant A had to do -- referred to municipalities that had a Serb majority, uncontested Serb majority, and Variant B referred to municipalities where Serbs were a minority group; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure what you mean by uncontested majority, but yes, the general outline; Variant A, Serb majority; Variant B, Serb minority.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Now, Variant A, I believe, is not is a contested concept, but Variant B implied that the territory of an existing municipality in which the Serbs were a minority, those parts where they lived alone were to be separated from the territory of the existing municipality and they were to become a Serb municipality, for instance, as we saw a few moments ago of Zvornik; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Variant B says that the measures are to be applied in those territories where the Serbs -- where they lived. But they never lived alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Madam, could you please answer my question. I'm trying to make this clearer for the Trial Chamber and not actually make it even more complicated. So is it true, we saw a few moments ago and we still actually have it before us on the screens - if we can just go back to page 2 of e-court - you can see that item 2 relates to -- refers to the areas of Zvornik municipality where this decision will be applicable, the decision to establish the Serb municipality of Zvornik. And I'm asking you very specifically: Does Variant B imply that those municipalities that have a Serb minority in them, the Serb municipality will only be established for those territories where Serbs lived; correct? So just in parts of those municipalities?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree in essence with you, but I want to make something clear, that Serbs lived -- that --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But, madam --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would just ask that the witness be allowed to answer. She's made it clear that although she agrees with part of it, she wishes to qualify that and she should be given the opportunity to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I do not wish to cut the witness at all. I just want to stream-line the witness. I will give her the opportunity to express herself and her views on the matter at any given moment, believe me. But I just want to explain this concept.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this case, madam, would you please -- I apologise for interrupting you, would you please go on and provide your full answer.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: My understanding is Variant B is to be applied only in those territories within the Variant B municipalities where the Serb population lived in a majority. But you said earlier alone, where the Serbs lived alone, and wherever Serbs lived, and even a minority -- Serb minority municipality would have Serbs in many parts of the territory. There was no part of the municipality that was purely Serb and no part that was purely non-Serb. But I agree, it is to be applied only in those parts of the territories where the Serbs were the majority population within a larger Serb minority municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Madam, Mrs. Hanson, can we take another look at this document, please. That's document P437. The last -- the last three lines of paragraph 2 state, after mentioning the municipal communes -- the local communes and settled places or inhabited places, it says "and also parts of local communes in the town, in the towns of -- in the areas of Srpska Varos, Zamlaza, Begusje or something like that, Versuje [phoen]. In other words, only parts of some town local communes will enter and become part of the Serb municipality of Zvornik; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And these parts are parts of city local communes where Serbs lived; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: My problem is with the phrase "where Serbs lived." Serbs lived throughout the municipality of Zvornik. I imagine -- from my knowledge of -- general knowledge of that area and of such documents, these are local communes in which the Serbs represent a majority population, but I am not going to say that only Serbs lived there and that Serbs lived only there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Madam, I'm grateful to you because you have now anticipated my next question. Thank you very much. So in other words, these are parts of local communes where Serbs lived as a majority group, and I'm not saying that the Serbs alone lived there, but they were the majority ethnic group; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's exactly what I was trying to clarify earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Well, finally we have a common understanding of this. Thank you. Let us now go back to P69, that's document Variant A and B. I see in your report --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we could just please pull it up on the screen -- or rather, Your Honour, I note the time, would this be a good time for a break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, if this is going to be a fairly lengthy exchange we can break now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am afraid so. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: May I proceed, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Hanson, just before the break I wanted to go back to P69 document about Variants A and B. I noticed that in your report, you did not consider or comment upon point 8 of the instructions. It's on page 6 in e-court. It's already up on the screen. It's the second degree of Variant A which reads: "In taking all these measures, make sure that national and other rights of members of all nations are respected and that they are later engaged in government organs established or to be established by the Assembly of the Serbian People in the municipality." It is a fact that you did not comment upon this in your report?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the contrary, I comment on it in paragraph 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, you are right. The thing that confused me was that in paragraph 16, you say that Crisis Staffs were exclusively Serbian organs established to defend the interests of the Serbian people. I am sorry. Are you maybe aware because you focused on these municipalities in the indictment, are you aware that Fadil Topcagic, a Muslim from Bosanski Samac, was a member of the Crisis Staff of the Samac municipality? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I have now page 10 of this document. In item 2 -- I believe in English it's also the same page in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Item 2 stipulated the obligation of these organs, or rather, all government bodies to comply with the federal constitution, federal laws, and other federal regulations, as well as republican regulations that do not contravene federal ones. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I think in several passages in your report, you emphasised that you had not succeeded in finding a legal ground for the establishment of these Crisis Staffs; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not found the use of the term "Crisis Staff" itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, when this is written in this document, did you explore perhaps what the author might have meant when he said compliance with federal legislation and republican legislation that is not contrary to federal laws?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my first section of the report, I indicate possible legal origins of this kind of body, but as I say, I was not able to find the use of the term "Crisis Staff" itself. This phrase of observing federal laws and Bosnian republic laws only so far as they do not contradict the federal laws. We see in many -- used a lot by various Serb organs and bodies at this time. This phrase I've seen in several places, so I'm familiar with it. But as I say, I did not find -- I was looking at the federal legislation for the collective bodies that could possibly be Crisis Staffs.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I hope you are not trying to say that this provision in number 2 was placed in this instruction without any reason whatsoever? I hope you are not trying to say that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not trying to say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right. My mistake then. Since you did not manage to find the term "Crisis Staffs," I believe in one of your testimonies you also said you did not find the term "War Presidency" anywhere in literature.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't believe I say that. If I could go back to that section of my report. Okay, they do not say "War Presidency" but they say "Presidency" in -- yes, so I did not find -- okay, those two sentence, as I indicated yesterday, were written by a colleague. I checked his references, I did not see the term "War Presidency." I did see reference to a collective Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right. So the situation is like this: You definitely did not find the term "Crisis Staff" or the term "War Presidency" in literature. You found some similar terms but not these two; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On that basis, you took the position that such organs, namely Crisis Staffs, were designed and put into operation by the Serbian Democratic Party in December 1991 precisely by virtue of this document, Variants A and B?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. You discussed the federal Law on the Basics of National Defence and Social Self-Protection which envisaged certain organs that call themselves commissions for national defence and social self-protection that were formed in municipalities under extraordinary circumstances, and that law, as well as another document that we will discuss in due course, explains their place and role, and I believe you described that in paragraph 7 and 8 of your report; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in essence, but I don't cite the federal law, I cite the republic law.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: At any rate, the federal Law on National Defence and Social Self-Protection is a systemic law adopted at the federal level in the former Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, and then, all the republics passed identical laws for the purposes of the republics at republic level?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is my understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Have you ever read the Law on the All People's Defence and Social Self-Protection, be it the republican law of Bosnia-Herzegovina or the federal law?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read parts of it, specifically the parts referring to these committees.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Would you tell me, Mrs. Hanson, have you heard about a document called "The Strategy of All People's Defence and Social Self-Protection"? Have you heard about it?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm familiar with the concept of All People's Defence and social self-protection. I have not read a specific document entitled that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, the strategy of All People's Defence and social self-protection, as it says in the preamble, is the fundamental doctrinal document and it was adopted by the Presidency on the 20th of May, 1987, by the Presidency of the SFRY, and that document explains the doctrine of All People's Defence, social self-protection, and stipulates in detail the provisions of the law. Are you familiar with it or do you know anything about it?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I'm familiar with the general concept of All People's Defence. I'm not familiar with that specific book and the specific provisions of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Since you are not a lawyer, it is your colleague who did the research into that documentation, and this document will certainly be an exhibit in this case. I will, therefore, not bore you or the Trial Chamber with individual provisions. Since, as you say, you are familiar with the concept of All People's Defence and social self-protection, you know that this concept envisaged compulsory establishment of commissions for All People's Defence and social self-protection in extraordinary circumstances on the territory of municipalities, be it in the republics or in the whole territory of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia; correct.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I say, I'm familiar with the legislation -- that these bodies were foreseen. The mandatory formation I'm not familiar with. I can't comment on it one way or another.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that every segment of society, beginning with schools, factories, health centres and such-like, let alone institutions of the state system, had the obligation to draft a plan of All People's Defence and social self-protection, the so-called Defence plan and to have a rapporteur for this subject and to nominate potential members of such commissions for All People's Defence and self-protection in the event of war. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I certainly know they were required to draft a plan and had a referent for those matters. The actual obligation to nominate members of committee I am not aware of, but it certainly seems a logical conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, isn't it true that these commissions for All People's Defence and self-protection in terms of their composition, powers, and role were very similar, if not identical, to the composition, powers and role of the Crisis Staffs?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I find great similarities.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Madam, didn't it seem logical to you that it is, in fact, these bodies that are referred to when Crisis Staffs are mentioned, although the name "commission" is avoided because that name was suggested or invokes the communist heritage. Whereas all these parties that established these things called themselves democratic, the Serbian Democratic Party, the Party of Democratic Action, the Croatian Democratic Union, et cetera. Didn't it seem logical to you that these parties wanted to break away from the communist legacy and that is why they named their bodies differently?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that there was an attempt separate from the communist legacy. I agree that the Crisis Staffs resemble these All People's Defence committees very much, but I've never seen it explicated -- and I rely on documents. I've never seen it explicated that, These are the same things, we're changing the name. And I simply go by what the Crisis Staffs called themselves and the way they operated, declaring themselves to be the municipal authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In one passage in your report or perhaps in your earlier evidence, I don't have the reference, I'm sorry, but you can confirm or deny what I'm going to say, you stated that it is not important how the bodies call themselves, whether it was a Crisis Staff or War Presidency or a war commission because all that you said in your report concerning Crisis Staff applies to all of them because they are basically identical bodies. I believe that's your paragraph 48.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Since you did say that, tell me why not apply the same thinking, the same analogy to Crisis Staffs, or rather -- sorry, strike that. Explain to me why you did not apply the same analogy to the relationship between commissions of All People's Defence and social self-protection and Crisis Staffs? I mean, that those were identical bodies in terms of powers, role, and composition.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was tasked to look at the Crisis Staffs in the Bosnian Serb municipalities. I did not observe these All People's Defence committees taking over in the place of Crisis Staffs, declaring themselves to be the municipal authority as Crisis Staffs did. I brought the Prosecution team's attention to the parallels with this earlier committee in the legislation, but I was writing on what Crisis Staffs did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right. But after all this time and after your examination and your evidence, you can agree with me now that between this committee, these commissions for All People's Defence, and social self-protection, and Crisis Staffs, there is a considerable analogy. They are practically identical in terms of role, powers and composition.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have agreed that they are identical. Even in my report I cite the example of Bosanski Novi where they say, We changed our self-defence -- our defence committee into a Crisis Staff. So I make that clear in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your report, Mrs. Hanson, you claim that the SDS by virtue of this Variant A and B initiated the establishment of Crisis Staffs of the SDS in December 1991; right?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In your view, did Mr. Karadzic and the Serbian Democratic Party have the same sort of influence on Alija Izetbegovic as the leader of the SDA and the leaders of the HDZ, the Croatian Democratic Union?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Did Karadzic have influence on Izetbegovic, no, not for ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, then, how do you explain the existence of completely identical bodies, in terms of name, powers, de facto action, on the opposite sides, on the Muslim side and the Croatian side, and on the territory of municipalities controlled by Muslims and Croats in Bosnia-Herzegovina? How do you explain that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not deny that there were Crisis Staffs on all sides. I say that in my report. I'm discussing in my report the Bosnian Serb Crisis Staffs, but I am aware that there were other Crisis Staffs.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Will you then agree with me that Crisis Staffs established on other sides, that is in other municipalities controlled by Bosnian Muslims and Croats, were completely identical bodies with the same powers, names, the same composition, and that they acted in exactly the same way as the Crisis Staffs of Bosnian Serbs in 1991 and 1992?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no basis to agree or disagree with you as I was tasked to look at Bosnian Serb Crisis Staffs. And I did not look at the other Crisis Staffs' operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Hanson, if you were aware that there were Crisis Staffs on other sides too, and it is quite clear that the SDS and Mr. Karadzic had no influence on Muslims and Croats, did you perhaps think that the uniformity of this concept comes from the legislative text on the basis of which they were formed, that is, the federal Law on All People's Defence and Social Self-Protection that was in place both in Bosnia-Herzegovina and in the Federation as a whole?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because the Bosnian Serb Crisis Staffs that I saw formed at this time, many of them clearly refer to Variant A and B as the basis for their formation. And of the ones that don't explicitly cite A and B, I do not see reference to the legislation on All People's Defence committees.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You know, as you confirmed in one of your previous testimonies, that the Crisis Staff of Bratunac municipality was formed identically with the same composition and all the other elements as all the others but that happened before the 19 December 1991 instruction; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the Crisis Staff of the SDS Municipal Board of Bratunac. Yes, it's the only one where I see a Crisis Staff formed previous to those instructions. However, when they do form the one in December, they are clearly referring to instructions from the SDS leadership on the formation of their Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, if I understood correctly, for awhile, sometime before December, they already had a Crisis Staff, and then after the 19 December instruction, they established one again, this time in keeping with the instruction, but there is no essential difference between the two?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the October Crisis Staff it is clearly based on the instructions of the Main Board of the SDS as well. So it's not spontaneously on their own initiative, it's on instructions from the expanded session of the SDS Main Board, so that is the only reference I find to that earlier Crisis Staff so I can't say with any certainty about its functioning or even membership compared to the later one, whether it's different or the same, I can't comment. It's such a brief mention in October, but I don't see any essential difference between them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: At any rate, it is your position that in both cases, the establishment of such a body followed the instructions of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is my position.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let me show you one document dated 21st September 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did we call up 1D00-5388.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Madam, this is a document which has in the heading "Presidency of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina," then we see the number, Sarajevo, 21 September 1991. These are minutes from the 35th Session of the Presidency of the Socialist Republic Bosnia-Herzegovina, and it says, among other people, there are president of the Presidency Alija Izetbegovic present, members of the Presidency, Biljana Plavsic, Stjepan Kljujic, Dr. Ejup Ganic, and some other people, in other words, all of the leadership of Bosnia-Herzegovina at that moment, 21st September. On page 2, did you see this document before?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may have. I don't recall specifically until I can see more of the subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: We see here under item 3 that it reads as follows: "The government of BH is requested to ensure in these crisis situation normal living conditions and so on and so forth, and then it says that Presidency member Biljana Plavsic did not agree with items one and two, and then it reads as follows. The Presidency formed the Crisis Staff composed of the following members: Dr. Ejup Ganic, member of the Presidency, staff coordinator, that's his function; then Dr. Biljana Plavsic; then Franjo Boras, master of sciences; and then Minister of the Interior, Alija Delimustafic; People's Defence minister, Jerko Doko; and the BH Territorial Defence commander, Lieutenant-General Drago Vukosavljevic. And then it says the seat of the Crisis Staff shall be on the premises of the Presidency and assisted by the services of the Presidency, appropriate ministries and other organs and organisations in the republic. So you see this portion that I've just read out?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In other words the Presidency of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina established a Crisis Staff of the Presidency as the highest organ of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina as early as September 1991, and its composition reflects absolutely the Crisis Staffs that are established pursuant to SDS instructions or, as we shall see later, Crisis Staffs established by the SDA and the HDZ. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that the composition is parallel to the other Crisis Staffs. I don't see in this document that the Crisis Staff is established as the highest organ.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. If you could now please look at the last page of this document. We see the signature of the president of the Presidency of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Mr. Alija Izetbegovic. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see a signature, yes. I assume it's Izetbegovic's.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D108, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I would now like to show you another document, but before I do that, let me ask you this: Do you know that before this day, the MUP of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina at the head of which was Mr. Alija Delimustafic, a Muslim, had adopted a decision on the establishment of a Crisis Staff whose specific task had to do with the possible arrest of Mr. Martic on the 8th of September, 1991. Are you aware of this, madam?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I am not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please pull up document 1D00-4569 on the screens. This is a document that we found containing the earliest date of a Crisis Staff being established based on the documents that we had at our disposal and access to. This is a document from the Municipal Assembly of Ljubuski. For your information let me say that this is part of Bosnia-Herzegovina which was under the control of Croat forces. The document bears the date 26th of August, 1991, and it reads as follows: "Decision to appoint members of Ljubuski municipality Crisis Staff." And then we see that there are 11 members appointed. And under item 2, it says the decision shall be published in the Official Gazette of Ljubuski municipality. Mrs. Hanson, reading this document, you can see under 3 that the presidents of Ljubuski Municipal Assembly is a member of this. Under 4 we see the chief of the public security station, it says public, "Javne Sigurnosti," because this is a Croatian translation, and under 5 is the commander of the Ljubuski Municipal Territorial Defence staff and then some other members. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, judging by its composition, this crisis too mirrors exactly the Crisis Staffs that were later to be established by, as you said, instructions from the SDS; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not exactly, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, tell me then who is missing here. We see that we have the president of the Municipal Assembly. We have the president of the Executive Board. Under number 1, we have the municipal Secretary-General administrator. Under 5, we have the commander of the Territorial Defence. We also have certain party members. So how does it differ from SDS Crisis Staffs?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say anyone was missing. I think it has members beyond the scope of the SDS Crisis Staffs such as the -- probably the director of the health centre, that's not unusual to see them on the later Crisis Staffs, but specifically, the representatives of the SDA and HDZ and the SDS -- HDS, sorry, were not members the SDS Crisis Staffs.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, madam, you just confirmed to me a little earlier that Mr. Fadil Topcagic, a Muslim from Bosanski Samac, was a member of the Crisis Staff in Bosanski Samac. Are you saying that he was a member of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but I don't know if he was on it as a member of the -- as a representative of the SDA or as a representative of his particular employment. I am aware that I've seen his name on the Crisis Staff minutes, but I'm just saying that I think it's a parallel to have political representatives on the Crisis Staffs. But that is the difference I see between an SDS Crisis Staff and these ones, is which parties are represented.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But wait a minute, the fact that it doesn't state what party the president of the Municipal Assembly belongs to, the president of the Executive Board or chairman of the executive committee, the secretary of the Secretariat, the chief and the commander, that does not imply that they are not members of the HDZ; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, their positions were mentioned there and not their party membership because that is something that is understood by implication, because the HDZ in Ljubuski, as one of the municipalities in Bosnia-Herzegovina where the Croatian population was in the majority, was a party that was a dominant party, a majority party in that territory?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a Municipal Crisis Staff which includes members of different political parties. The SDS Crisis Staffs as formed on the A and B instructions included only SDS members and included members purely for their function within the party and not in the municipality, such as members of the SDS Main Board, deputies to the National Assembly. This one includes different parties, that's the distinction I was trying to make.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, let's go through this slowly, we will come to that. It is an uncontested fact, and I believe you mention it in your report - I assume it's uncontested - that the SDS Crisis Staffs were only in existence in a very short limited period of time, and that at the point where the Assemblies are formed in these municipalities, at the same time different bodies, government bodies would be formed in the municipality as well; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see that in the -- that pattern in the documentary evidence at all. I see the Crisis Staffs --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: We will come back to that a little later, if that's not a problem with you. I don't want to interrupt you. If you wish to answer now, please provide it, but as I've already said, we will revisit this issue. But would you like to comment further?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just would say that I see Assemblies declared in December in some places along with the Crisis Staffs, but I see the Crisis Staffs staying -- staying and becoming the municipal authorities and the Municipal Assemblies not taking over until the summer of 1992. That's the pattern I generally see.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Madam, let us go back to this document. If we look at it, it is uncontested that the most significant members or representatives of the authorities are present here and members of this staff in Ljubuski municipality; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D109, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Bearing in mind your comment regarding this document, 1D109, the Crisis Staff in Ljubuski municipality document, I would now like to put to you a document from the Croatian Democratic Union of Bosnia-Herzegovina, document number 002842. 1D00-2842.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please pull it up on the screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Hanson, this is a document from the Croatian Democratic Union of Bosnia-Herzegovina, that is the Croatian ethnic, as it were, party, which was au par with the Serbian Democratic Party and the Party of Democratic Action in Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1990 and 1991, and all these three national parties had their own candidates in the elections in 1990. Now you can see in the heading that it says the Security Council of the BH HDZ strictly confidential. The date we see is 18 September 1991. And it reads as follows, title: "Conclusions of the Security Council of the BH HDZ held on 18 September 1991." And then it says under conclusions under item 1: "The present Security Council shall be called the BH HDZ Crisis Staff in the future. Its members shall be," and then it lists, Mr. Kljujic, Mr. Boban, Mr. Kvesic, Jerko Doko, he was the minister of national defence in the socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina government. Then we see Dario Kordic, Kost roman, Bruno Stojic. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: These individuals whose names I just read out were the leaders, doubtlessly, of the Croatian Democratic Union and of the Croatian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina at the time; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my understanding, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Now, in the second paragraph it says: "In addition to the executive and political Crisis Staff the staff must form a specialist command body which shall be a specialist military body directly responsible for certain operations." And then it says in paragraph 3: "The Crisis Staff shall begin its duties immediately and is to lead the entire defence system of the Croatian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina and ensure the acquisition of armaments." And under paragraph 4: "The chairman of the Crisis Staff is Stjepan Kljujic and the deputy chairman is -- rather, his deputy is Mate Boban." Can you see all that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Please tell me, did you have occasion to see this document earlier, while you were drafting your report?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't be sure. I probably would have seen it because it would have come up on the hit for Crisis Staff, but I did not use it because it's not a Bosnian Serb Crisis Staff. It's not familiar to me, but I may well have seen it just because it would have come up on the search.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
