utterances.text: Well, that's all very well, but the earlier document that I presented to you, you felt the need to say that this was a Municipal Crisis Staff, but here we see that a party is establishing a Crisis Staff. So I believe this is a very clear parallel to the positions that you set forth when discussing Variant A and B documents and the role of the SDS in establishing SDS Crisis Staffs; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's parallel.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us now take a look at page 2, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, it says under item 2: "In the event of armed conflict in the territory where the Croatian people are in the majority, the Crisis Staffs shall take over all the duties of the authorities in the municipalities, and the work of the BH HDZ shall cease temporarily until the threat of war has passed, that is, until the Crisis Staff considers it to have passed." Can you see any difference between this and the instructions issued by the SDS? Isn't it true that the SDS, too, says that the Crisis Staffs shall take over all the duties in municipalities, all the powers in municipalities, and that once the conflict broke out, all party activities shall cease. Can you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It sounds to me more like the instructions issued by the president of the government, Djeric, in April 1992, but it certainly seems parallel to what I see -- how the SDS Crisis Staffs and then the RS Crisis Staffs are operating. I'd have to check A and B to see if -- I don't recall that exact wording in A and B, but it is in the Djeric's instructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 4, in the last sentence, it says that the Crisis Staffs have to understand the urgency of the serious situation and exert or direct all their activities to the Defence of the Croatian people. Isn't there a similar formulation in Variant A and B instructions and I'm referring to the preamble itself where it says that all its activities will be directed at the defence of the Serbian people and their interests and their defence, the defence of the Serbian people; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, A and B says it's -- carry out the mobility in defence of the interests of Serbian people, so it's similar phrasing, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Under 2 it says, in this document: "Crisis Staffs shall be formed urgently for three regional communities of the Croatian Democratic Union of Bosnia-Herzegovina," and then it mentions the regions of Travnik, Posavina, and --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the third region.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And it says then that the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: The interpreters are asking you to repeat your last sentence because they didn't get the name of the municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise to the Trial Chamber and to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I've said the Sarajevo regional community of the HDZ of Bosnia and Herzegovina shall be directly co-ordinated by the republican Crisis Staff. That's the reading in the document; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You can see under item 3, that: "Crisis Staffs must also be urgently established on the same principles as those of the republican and regional Crisis Staffs," and then it says it is advised that chairmen of Municipal Crisis Staffs be presidents of municipals if they were appointed by the BH HDZ, otherwise chairman of the Executive or Municipal Boards of the BH HDZ. Can you see that, madam?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So the distinction between this concept and the SDS concept is really non-existent; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are strong parallels.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In item 4 it says: "The appointed persons representing the BH HDZ in governing bodies have the duty to continue carrying out their tasks conscientiously, giving priority to the interests of the Croatian people." And then under item 7, it says: "All municipal authorities where the BH HDZ has an absolute or relative majority is responsible to compile a list stating the state of food, medical and sanitary supplies, state of weapons and ammunition supplies, power plants, military locations, manpower, and programs of Defence and civilian protection." So, Ms. Hanson, aren't these obligations identical to the ones that are envisaged in the Variant A and B instructions of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are very similar. Really quite parallel.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And one final point, in item 8, it says: "Municipalities are recommended not to send recruits to the army and to forbid any mobilisation of forces except for mobilisation organised through our own Crisis Staffs." In other words, here the Crisis Staffs of the Croatian Democratic Union even includes its regional Crisis Staffs in the work relating to the mobilisation; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Where there is a comment saying that this document is strictly confidential, and among other things, there is a chart provided of -- an organisational chart of Crisis Staffs which we can find on the next page. So as you can see, this document too is strictly confidential, although we could see that on the first page as well; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So I have shown you now some of the key documents, and I will now also follow this up with documents that were produced in the field on the basis of these. Madam, this document is from September 1991. We've also seen the Presidency document also from September 1991, and the document entitled "Variant A and B instructions" is dated December 1991. All these three documents absolutely speak to the establishment of Crisis Staffs. There is nothing else that they discuss. They all actually mention the establishment of Crisis Staffs. So are you now trying to tell us here that a person who -- such as you, who is interested and doing research into Crisis Staffs and has a problem to determine where the term "Crisis Staff" comes from, how is it possible that you did not review these documents as well, or at least mention these documents in your report, saying there are documents coming from the Presidency dated September 1991, and also HDZ documents as early as September 1991, as well as SDA documents from sometime in 1991, which also are used to establish Crisis Staffs, as the document that you discuss in your report, but which actually predate by two months the SDA instructions -- SDS instructions. So how is it that this did not find its way into your report, and how is it that you showed no interest in these documents while you were preparing your report? Could you please tell us that.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I indicate in my report that there were Crisis Staffs on the Croatian and Bosnian side. I say in my report that I have not found the term "Crisis Staff" in the legislation. I am aware that it was used in popular terminology, but I say that I do not find the phrase in the legislation. These are instances of it -- certainly of Crisis Staffs being formed, but not an indication of the legislative basis and this last document, I don't believe I've seen. I said it would have come up in a search but I haven't seen such an explication of the Croatian Crisis Staffs, so I cannot say that I've seen it. Once again, my tasking was to explain to the Prosecution team Bosnian Serb Crisis Staffs. I don't deny the existence of other Crisis Staffs. Never have.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It seems to me that the wording that you are using in your report and in your evidence was that Crisis Staffs on the other sides were established in the course -- during the war, but nowhere in your report do you explicitly say or even mention that Crisis Staffs had been established by the Presidency, the HDZ, and the SDA, even before the SDS instructions of 19 December were issued; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Had I been tasked to look at HDZ Crisis Staffs, I certainly would find this document very interesting. But I do not mention the Presidency Crisis Staff, correct, I do not mention it in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Madam, now we will go back to square one. When I asked you whether you considered that the role of an expert witness is to present their knowledge in an objective manner that will assist the Trial Chamber in their decisions, you -- and whether you consider that these documents, or documents such as these, provide a more balanced picture of the situation which is something that you are discussing in your report?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said before, there are many, many, many documents that provide a balanced situation -- a balanced view of the situation. My report is devoted to Bosnian Serb Crisis Staffs and it could perhaps -- had people felt the need to learn more about whether this was a brand new term and whether there were Crisis Staffs on other sides, yes, I could have given more attention to that. But that was not my tasking and that was not an issue that emerged as something that needs explaining or attention since it was -- since I was tasked to look at Bosnian Serb Crisis Staffs.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mrs. Hanson. Since it is our job here to establish the responsibility of our defendants, in other words, we do not have to limit ourselves to certain segments as you do, I propose that this document be admitted into admitted into evidence as an exhibit in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D110, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Hanson, I would like to show you a document that relates to one of the municipalities that is scheduled in the indictment. Document 1D00-4000. In other words, 1D00-4000. This is a document that shows that the previous instruction of the Bosnia-Herzegovina HDZ, that this is actually the implementation of that decision. This is the Municipal Board of Kotor Varos, the Municipal Board of the Croatian Democratic Union of Kotor Varos dated 16th March 1992, and it is stated there that a Crisis Staff is being established. The decision is dated the 8th of March, and we see the members of the Crisis Staff there, there are five individuals, as well as a stamp of the Croatian Democratic Union of Kotor Varos; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say with certainty that I have but I know that I -- I can see from its ERN that it's from a selection -- from an index I've searched.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It's already Exhibit 1D23.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, thank you very much. I apologise. Could we now please show the witness document 1D00-3109. This is a document dated 7 April 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It has a similar ERN number, so my question to you is: Have you seen this document? This document also comes from the Municipal Board of the Kotor Varos Croatian Democratic Union confirming that a Crisis Staff consisting of five members was established in March, and then it mentions certain problems that they had, that there was another Crisis Staff established subsequently. Can you see this document?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember or have you had occasion to review this document in the course of your work?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once again, it's from an index I've searched, but once again, I was look at SDS and Serb municipality Crisis Staffs so I may well have seen it, taken a look at it, identified it as an HDZ document and not looked at it further.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I could be heard on that. I'm just wondering where we are going with this. We've had documents that are put to her from other ethnic group Crisis Staffs, and they are addressing a certain point about where the phrase "Crisis Staff" came from. Now, it seems we've gone beyond that, and is my learned colleague simply going to put forward document after document of other ethnic group Crisis Staffs; and if so, how is that really relevant to our case. They are not part of our case. It sort of sounds like it's a -- a sort of a tu quoque defence here. If we can find out the relevance of where we are going with these documents, I would ask that perhaps that could be explained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, as I understand the thrust of Mr. Zecevic's line so far is that the quality of the expert report on which the Prosecution is relying is weakened by failure to have taken into consideration these other matters, but I take your point that there comes a point at which one must draw the line. Mr. Zecevic, hasn't your point been made sufficiently?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, well, I'm ready to explain, but I think it would be proper that the witness is excused before -- before I can provide you with my explanation why am I pursuing this line and I don't know, maybe if you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, we are five minutes short of the break. We would excuse you now and deal with this matter and ask you to return for 12.25. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it is absolutely the Defence position that the fact that a so-called expert did not feel it necessary to, as far as we see it, consider these very important documents which are important to understand the problem, the subject matter in this case, and since this expert witness did not feel it even necessary to mention these documents in her report, it is our position that this absolutely weakens the value, if not the factual value of this report, but in any case, not a single conclusion from this report can actually stand based on these documents. And especially, Your Honours, because from these documents -- from these documents we can see that Crisis Staffs, the roles of Crisis Staffs, and all those things that Crisis Staffs actually did in territories which were under Serbian control were identical in every sense to what the other two communities did and how they proceeded and what their Crisis Staffs in territories under their control did. And for these reasons, because the establishment of Crisis Staffs and their role is an important part of the Prosecutor's theory on the joint criminal enterprise, I believe that these facts and these documents are really a significant basis for the Defence to build their position that such a joint criminal enterprise was non-existent. And it is for this reason that I'm trying to tender these documents and try and put them to the alleged expert witness of the Prosecution who came here to provide her expertise on Crisis Staffs and who is absolutely qualified, as least in that sense, to discuss these documents, or to comment them and for these documents to be admitted because if this witness is qualified to comment on documents of the Serbian Crisis Staffs, then she is certainly qualified to also comment on the documents of the other side because -- so that is our position and this is where my line of questioning is leading. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I could be heard on that to respond to my learned colleague's comments. First of all, he's raised a couple of issues and what I would like to say, first of all, is that Ms. Hanson is not an alleged expert witness. Your Honours have determined that she is an expert witness, so I just wanted to put that on the record. Secondly, my learned colleague has stated that the failure to include these documents is a weakness in Ms. Hanson's report. As she has said repeatedly on the stand, she was tasked with preparing a report on Bosnian Serb Crisis Staffs. She's also said that in that report, she acknowledges that the other ethnic communities did form Crisis Staffs. She didn't take that any further as she didn't feel it was particularly relevant to this report. Beyond that. Now, my learned colleague has raised that issue with her and has shown her documents, but to continue showing more and more documents, I don't believe it advances that particular issue any further, as to the weakness of her report. She's already answered the -- the questions that have been put to her about that and why there aren't documents like these in there. Beyond that, Your Honour, I still don't see the relevance to our case of actions that were taken by Crisis Staffs of the other ethnic groups. The JCE in this case involves Bosnian Serb Crisis Staffs, and the fact that Crisis Staffs from other ethnic groups may have been forming, may have been taking actions, isn't relevant to our case here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, I fully understand your point, but my question would be that to the extent in which the Crisis Staffs formed by the Bosnian Serb leadership in Bosnia and Herzegovina became an instrument in the commission of the crimes for which your client stands accused, then what is the Chamber supposed -- or rather, which conclusion is the Chamber, in your view, supposed to draw from the fact that Crisis Staffs were also formed by the Muslims and by the Croats, and that indeed at some point the republican leadership formed joint Crisis Staffs? I see your point, but which conclusion are you getting at in drawing our attention to this?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I don't know if I would be ready to fully answer that question at this point, but I can certainly do that after the break. But as a first thing that crosses my mind is that I would expect that this line of examination -- cross-examination and the in the future in your Defence case and these documents will show to the Trial Chamber that there is no pattern which is exclusively linked to the SDS or the Serbian Crisis Staffs. That the pattern, that the pattern basically derives out of the essence of these organs doesn't matter if they are Muslim, if they are Croatian, or Serbian. The essence is that basically by this concept of All People's Defence, these small -- these small Crisis Staffs were given immense, immense power in the territory and that power by itself corrupted the performance of these Crisis Staffs. And they -- they themselves got involved into the crimes, into whatever, expulsions. This is the suggestion of the Prosecutor's case, that this pattern is obviously a plan by the Serbs to forcibly expel, murder and all that, commit crimes against humanity. Now, when we see all these documents, you will see yourself that it comes out of the essence of these organs. It doesn't have anything to do with any plan. I'm not suggesting that the Muslims or Croats had any plan, or Serbs. So I'm saying that this will -- we tried to show to the Trial Chamber that that is the problem, and that is the problem, and the consequence of that problem is what happened in the territory, unfortunately. Unfortunately, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Do I understand you correctly if your point is that the widespread commission of crimes committed with the assistance or the participation somehow of the Crisis Staffs, that the commission of these crimes were not a result of any plan from the top, but was a result purely of the fact that they -- that these organs were established and were given too much power, and so it was -- it just happened. Is that your point?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Exactly, Your Honours, because if it was a plan, then this plan will apply to Croatian communities under the control of the HDZ, and to Muslim communities as well. Therefore, if the Crisis Staffs and the units in these territories were committing the very same crimes, then I don't know. You will have to decide whether the plan which somebody like Karadzic or SDS created, was followed in Ljubuski, was followed in the territory which was controlled by the SDA and HDZ, and why is that? I mean, that is my position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Your Honour, our position is that there may well have been Crisis Staffs formed in the other ethnic communities, they may even have been part of the JCE or some sort of plan such as we are alleging in regards to the Bosnian Serb Crisis Staffs, but that's not an issue before this Trial Chamber. It's not something which is -- Your Honours are really in a position to pass judgement on or to say there's any relevance to what we are looking at here. I still don't see how this evidence coming in is going to advance the case any further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We'll return in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, during the break, Mr. Zecevic and myself and also in the background, Mr. Pantelic, discussed the issue that's arisen. To what extent should evidence of Crisis Staffs relating to the Croats and the Muslims be admissible in this case. And of course, our position is that it is getting near to a tu quoque defence and it's impossible for Your Honours to evaluate the significance of these documents without hearing all the evidence that surrounds them; but we hope that we may be able to perhaps cut matters short if Your Honours give us an opportunity to consider that. I know that we're not sitting -- no Court is sitting tomorrow morning, because I understand there's a plenary. And therefore, we would like the -- to use the opportunity to discuss the matter generally within the Office of the Prosecutor, in particular, with those who are doing cases which, if you like, are the other side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Prlic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Exactly, Prlic in particular. To see whether we can reach some kind of consensus which may obviate the need for Mr. Zecevic to continue on this line. I understand he is prepared to move to a different topic on that basis and then come back to it if we can't reach agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours. I mean, we hope that that satisfied the requirement of the Trial Chamber to, well, not to take the position on the objection that my colleague has made, and we are trying to amicably sort this situation. If it would be possible tomorrow morning, and I will continue then with other matters in course of my cross-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And I've asked Mr. Zecevic if he could be very kind and give us 15 minutes at the end to raise the matter of documents again, I am afraid, the admission thereof.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, while the witness is entering court, can I move the Trial Chamber to admit the last document that I commented with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: 3109, is that it?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: 3109, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D111, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Hanson, over the break I hope we succeeded in finding a modality of dealing with this issue, and in keeping with the understanding we reached with our learned friends from the Prosecution, I will continue with other topics. You are probably aware, Ms. Hanson, that the inter-party agreement between the SDA, SDS and the HDZ -- let me first ask you this: You know that these three ethnic-based parties came out at the elections together in 1991, in the first multiparty elections, with the common objective of defeating the communist party; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: These three parties had between them a certain inter-party agreement; right?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not familiar with the specific agreement to which you are referring.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But I suppose you know from other facts that in keeping with that agreement, they adopted a principle whereby a party that got the majority of votes in a certain municipality would appoint the president of the municipality, and the second-ranking party would get the post of chairman of the Executive Board and so on. Do you know of that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's my general understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So if we take a municipality where the greatest number of votes were won by the Serbian Democratic Party, then the SDS would provide the president of the municipality; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the usual pattern.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: At the same time, according to that logic of things or the usual pattern, as you call it, the candidate for the president of the municipality nominated by the Serbian Democratic Party or any other party would usually be the president of the board of that party in a particular town?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Usually, but it's not always the rule.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: We agree about that, yes, usually. Then after the elections in 1990, we had a common situation wherein the president of the board of the victorious party would be elected president of that municipality, to sum up.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: My knowledge here is restricted to the municipalities relevant to the SDS. I can't speak to other municipalities. But in general, that's my understanding, but it's -- as you say, it's not always the rule.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: We have quite enough evidence to demonstrate that. I'm not asking you to confirm, I'm just discussing the general situation. Thus, at the moment when these Crisis Staffs are established, under the instructions, and as we have seen it happened always everywhere, the president of the party board would become president of the Crisis Staff; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not always everywhere, but generally, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So in a certain way, we have a concurrence of functions in one personality. One person can be, or rather, is at the same time president of the board of the party, president of the Crisis Staff of that party, and president of the municipality; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Since we have agreed on that, let us look at the chronology of events. In December 1991, these instructions are given to establish SDS Crisis Staffs. And one of the tasks of the Crisis Staffs are to form Assemblies of the Serbian People in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Assemblies of the Serbian People within the municipalities, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Now, on 9 January 1992, the Assembly of the Serbian People issues a declaration on the establishment of Republika Srpska; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That declaration on the establishment of Republika Srpska is followed by the adoption of the constitution of Republika Srpska on the 28th of February?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So at the moment when the constitution of Republika Srpska is adopted, towards the end of February 1992, the territory of Republika Srpska had already been designated, the constitutional order, the state system had already been identified, and the authorities are now to be established, on the republic level, the government, the Presidency, the Assembly already exists, and the authorities on lower levels on the ground; right?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe the council of ministers was already formed before the constitution was adopted, and as we see, the Municipal Assemblies are -- some of them formed the regions, formed all before the end of February, but this is when the state was taking form at the highest level with the decisions of the Assembly on the constitution. That we see the organs forming at the highest level.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I'm trying to rely on what you've already said in your evidence. It is a fact that not all Assemblies of the Serbian People were formed in the period from December through end February 1992 in the territory?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, not all.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Some were formed in May and in June even 1992?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where I see an actual Serb municipality or Municipal Assembly separating from an existing municipality, it was generally carried out much earlier than June. What we see is those -- some municipalities where the Serbs had an overwhelming majority didn't feel as much need to rename or take some of the steps indicated in A and B simply because their authority was -- they controlled the municipal organs and didn't need to form parallel ones. So in those cases you might not see something called a Serb municipality until later. By later, I mean at the time you mention, May or June.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm only trying to clarify one particular fact which I don't think is completely clear. Those party-led Crisis Staffs formed under these instructions. At the moment when organs of Republika Srpska at municipal level are formed, such as the Municipal Assembly and the Executive Board, at that moment, the Crisis Staffs, because they are party organs, not state organs, cease to have any influence on state organs; do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Madam, Crisis Staffs, there must be a distinction between Crisis Staffs of the SDS and Crisis Staffs of the municipality. You've said so yourself and you say so in the report. Is that correct, is there such a distinction?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I indicate in my report, there's a great deal of evidence to see -- to show an overlap between those two, that when they are acting as Municipal Crisis Staffs, that is Crisis Staffs of the Municipal Assembly, they still use the party stamp, use the party head letter, don't make an important distinction. We saw in the report on the work of the Kljuc Crisis Staff that they saw a perfect continuity between SDS Crisis Staff, Municipal Assembly Crisis Staff, Municipal Assembly War Presidency, I see the continuity in the evidence. I see a difference in how it is presented, a difference in terminology, that they, as I've indicated by April we see them acting as declaring themselves to be the Municipal Assembly Crisis Staff, but I don't see discontinuity in the makeup, in the tasks, in how they viewed themselves. And moreover, these are the Crisis Staffs of the Serbian municipalities, not of the pre-existing municipality -- municipal organs as established after the elections.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Madam, I'm sorry, I didn't want to interrupt you to avoid objections, but my question was really very simple and you are giving me a half-page answer. I'm kindly asking you to concentrate on the question alone and give me a precise answer. I'm not asking you about the continuity or discontinuity. That's not the issue. We will come to that perhaps later. I'm just asking you, since you say that there is a continuity, if there is a continuity, that means that there is a link between two different organs, where one organ is the Crisis Staff of the party and the other organ is the Crisis Staff of the municipality. Just tell me, is it the case that there were Crisis Staffs of the party and Crisis Staffs of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The municipality -- the Serbian municipality was also a creation of the SDS and I do not see a difference between the Crisis Staff of the party and the Crisis Staff of the Serbian municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I suppose, madam, that the municipality is a creation of the Serbian people, not of the party. The party just expresses the will of the people?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The municipality or the Serbian municipality. We see the Serbian municipality being formed by -- on the directions of the SDS party.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, madam, that's because 99 per cent of Serbian voters, 99 per cent of Serbian electorate voted for the platform of the Serbian Democratic Party, voted for that party, just as Croats and Muslims voted for their own national parties. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: 99 per cent seems large to me because there were other parties beside the national party, so I'm not prepared to say it was 99 per cent of Serbian voters voted SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But in any case, the majority of Serbian voters did vote SDS; right?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Are you trying to say that the Serbian Democratic Party imposed on the Serbian people against their will the establishment of Serbian municipalities in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, thank you, finally. So the Serbs in their majority placed their trust at the elections in the Serbian Democratic Party. The SDS has the majority in the parliament, the Assembly of the Serbian People; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those are two different things. The elections were to the Assembly of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina or to the -- if you are talking about those elections, and that's different from the Assembly of the Serbian People.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Madam, the elections in 1990 were for the joint Assembly. Most Serbian votes were given to the SDS. After that, in January 1992, the Serbian people formed the Assembly of the Serbian People -- sorry, it wasn't January. The Assembly of the Serbian People that had been formed already adopts a declaration establishing Republika Srpska; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That parliament that took the decision to establish Republika Srpska is the Assembly of the Serbian People where the SDS has the absolute majority; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let's come back to the beginning of my question where we seem to have gotten stuck. On the 28th of February, the constitution of Republika Srpska is passed and after that the organs of Republika Srpska are beginning to be set up in keeping with the constitutional arrangement.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said before, you see some of them before the 28th of February, such as the council of ministers, such as the Serbian Municipal Assemblies.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Madam, the council of ministers is a provisional advisory body formed just before the government was appointed, and it lasted for another month after the formation of the government of Republika Srpska and then it ceased to exist; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Madam, government bodies cannot be established before a constitution is passed, a constitution of a country which sets down its state and territorial functions; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: This Republika Srpska was a new creation and was to a large extent writing its own rules. I don't see that there's a contradiction to first form organs and declare your territory and then write a constitution.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very well, but be it as it may, a vast majority of the government bodies in the territory of Republika Srpska were established in March, April, and May of 1991 [as interpreted]; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: If by government you mean at the republic level, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just correction to transcript, page 67, line 3, witness -- question was May 1992, not 1991, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Madam, at the moment when in the territory where government bodies have been established, and I mean the Assembly, the Executive Board of a municipality, so when in such a territory a conflict breaks out, at that point in time a Crisis Staff would be established in that municipality; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not the pattern that I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Madam, yesterday you commented on and today as well, and a few moments ago you mentioned quotas or the key, and we --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Or Kljuc, the municipality of Kljuc, interpreter correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And we saw here a report that was submitted to the Municipal Assembly in Kljuc. Do you recall that document?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please bear with me. I want to try and find that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is under tab 38 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: 39, I believe. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No, actually you are correct, it is 39.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the declaration. 41. 41.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will provide the page reference in just a moment, I apologise. That is 65 ter 813 and this document was assigned a P number yesterday, but I can't find it right now.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P451.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 431.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Madam, this is a report --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please pull it up on the screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This a report on the work of the Crisis Staff, and then in parenthesis War Presidency, Municipal Assembly in Kljuc in the period 15th of May, 1992, up until the present. And then at the bottom it says July 1992. Do you recall us discussing this document yesterday?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And when speaking about this document yesterday, you actually used this document to show that there was continuity between the Crisis Staff of the SDS which then became the Crisis Staff of the municipality and then became the War Presidency. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Now, here at the very beginning of the document, on page 2, we see the following words: "The Crisis Staff which was set up at the Executive Board of the Kljuc Serbian Democratic Party on the 23rd of December, 1991, in mid-May," and here they mean 1999, "was expanded at the meeting to include a certain number of representatives of the local authority and was transformed into the Crisis Staff of the Kljuc Municipal Assembly at a meeting held on 14 May 1992 because there were no conditions and prerequisites to call a Municipal Assembly meeting to elect and endorse members of the Crisis Staff of the Municipal Assembly." Ms. Hanson, from this, it is clear that there are two different Crisis Staffs in existence; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are not in existence at the same time. The Crisis Staff of the SDS becomes the Crisis Staff of the Municipal Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But, Ms. Hanson, it says that it is to be expanded, that the current SDS staff is to be expanded and transformed. That's what it says in the document.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: From which it follows that the Crisis Staff of the SDS with a number of government representatives that were added now becomes the municipal Crisis Staff; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Now, tell me, isn't it true that on the 7th of May, 1992, and we saw this document as well yesterday, the newly established Serbian municipality of Kljuc was just established?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where did we see that?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I will show you that document as well. You saw it yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, please bear with me. That's document 65 ter 795. This document was assigned, I believe, number 438?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: If I may be of assistance, this is Exhibit P450.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Madam, do you see that? You actually said that we can see in capital letters Autonomous Region of Bosanska Krajina because it was on that day that the Kljuc municipality actually joined this autonomous region?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document which says Crisis Staff of the municipality of Kljuc, although the date is the 7th of May which indicates that even before that date they gave in the report, the SDS Crisis Staff was calling itself the Kljuc municipal Crisis Staff, but I don't see here the -- I'm familiar with this document, I don't see that it states that the Serbian municipality of Kljuc was just established here. That's what I'm looking for.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It is possible that I also had in mind some other documents or exhibits that we had occasion to see here and which is why I recall this date as the date when the Serbian municipality of Kljuc was established. But I thought this was a fact that you were aware of. If not, I will find those documents and put them to you. Madam, if we go back to the earlier -- the previous document, where the SDS Crisis Staff was transformed to become the Municipal Assembly Crisis Staff and where it said, in the paragraph that I referred to earlier, that at a meeting held on the 14th of May of that year, the Crisis Staff of Kljuc municipality was established; in other words, on the 14th of May. And it provides the reasons saying that there had been no preconditions and prerequisites that would allow this to be done earlier, to establish Crisis Staffs of Municipal Assemblies. So my question to you again is whether -- do you still maintain that even in this particular case, these were not two [Realtime transcript read in error "too"] different organs?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I just pointed out, the previous document shows that there was something calling itself the Crisis Staff of the municipality before the 14th of May. I agree that in abstract technical terms the Crisis Staff of a party should be different from the Crisis Staff of a Municipal Assembly. As in practical terms as shown in the evidence which I've looked at in the Serbian municipalities, I do not see a distinction between the two. I see a great deal of overlap, confusion of terminology, confusion of the procedures and the emphasis on continuity such as in the third paragraph which says the Crisis Staff met as an organ of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm glad that at least in this abstract and technical terms we can agree. My question to you is: Isn't your misperception of this being one and the same organ in continuity, doesn't that misconception actually arise from the very fact that the same people were in fact members of one and then the other organ? Isn't that the key element of continuity that you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm referring to the continuity perceived by the members of the Crisis Staff. Karadzic himself said, You remember A and B at the beginning of the war, we had our Crisis Staffs. And he is referring to A and B, and they were the powers of the municipality. He said, We held power firmly thanks to A and B, so that's the continuity I see from the documents themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours, just a quick correction to the transcript. It's minor, but it does change the meaning somewhat. Page 70, line 25, the last word is "too," t-o-o, and I believe it should be t-w-o.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Line 23.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Madam, when you refer to the statement by Mr. Karadzic, do you mean the statement before the Assembly in 1995 that was read out to you yesterday?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That's in tab 5, I believe, in your binder. The document is P438.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have it on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You have been shown this document and you commented on it, the portion that you reiterated a few moments ago, where Karadzic was bragging about Variant A and B producing results and so on and so forth, and you said that this was an Assembly session where military issues were discussed. Now, madam, isn't it true that this was one of the most serious episodes in the history of Republika Srpska where the well-known rift between the then president of Republika Srpska, Mr. Karadzic, and the army of Republika Srpska, in other words, General Mladic, actually occurred; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The conflict was ongoing through the period from April through August 1995, but that was one of the issues at this Assembly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Madam, and I put it to you that 98 per cent of this document actually refers to this conflict, the clash between Karadzic and Mladic. And I would now like to read out to you --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the page number.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Page 184, where I will quote to you what President Karadzic said.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So page 184 of the Serbian text, and I assume that it is on the same page in the English version. 184. It's probably page 185 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It begins with the words: "The political show-down in Bosnia ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, I keep saying 184 and not 83. Page 83. It says on top of the page 184.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In any case, in order to save time, I will read the document to you. Madam, you have it in front of you, that was under tab number 5. It reads as follows: This is Karadzic speaking and he is quoting the last paragraph on this page.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, that is the right page in the Serbian version and I assume it's the same page in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Karadzic is quoting the US news daily report of 20th April 1992, and he says that this report is entitled "Political Clashes In Bosnia," and it says as follows. So it's Karadzic quoting the US news daily report: "The current Muslim offensives [Realtime transcript read in error "offences"] against Serb positions in central Bosnia has resulted in a clash for power within the leadership of Bosnian Serbs. Apparently Radovan Karadzic was defeated. Serb observers who recently visited Pale and representatives of Bosnian Serbs report that the military leadership, headed by Ratko Mladic, actually managed to control the president because they felt that his leadership was misleading them too frequently. He may give public pronouncements approved by the army, but no more than that, the sources report. He is politically dead." Do you recall or did you have occasion to read that part of this document? These are Karadzic's words and you should have been able to see it and read it. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, before the witness is answer, I don't think that on page 73, line 19, it's correct. I think instead of "offences," maybe it's "offensive" or maybe "military action." Maybe I'm ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, all right, in any case, we can see the original quotation in the document. I don't want to waste any more of our time because we have to actually finish earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So tell me, madam, have you read this part of Karadzic's remarks?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read it now. I'm not sure whether I read it before or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I will tell you, or rather, I will read another portion from it. We have a minute or two left. So on the next day, the session of the next day --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours. I'm very sorry to interrupt but I just want to point out that what we are seeing on the screens, the English page is not matching up to the B/C/S. The English runs much later. I only have the portion in front of me that I used with Ms. Hanson yesterday so I can't direct it to the right page, but I just want to make it clear that what you are seeing does not match up.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Your Honours, since it is time for us to wrap up because Ms. Korner had asked to be given an opportunity to address you, I would like to finish now and I will provide the pages, the corresponding English pages tomorrow. Thank you, Ms. Hanson, that will be all for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, thank you. We are -- you are now excused as a witness to return to this Chamber at 2.15 tomorrow. The Chamber will not be sitting in the morning. The usher will now escort you from the courtroom while we deal with some other matters. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And my usual warnings are repeated so to the extent that it is redundant to say so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm sorry to raise the ever-vexed question of the admission of documents. It really -- it's two separate but related matters. Your Honour, the first is this: The list that Mr. Dobbyn gave the Court was only the list of documents he was specifically going to put to Ms. Hanson. But additionally, of course, there are many documents which are on the 65 ter list submitted by the Prosecution which are footnoted in her report. We went back to check whether there was a ruling on how we were supposed to have these documents admitted and I don't know whether Your Honours had printed out, I am afraid the e-mail was sent this morning to the Court, to what His Honour Judge Harhoff said in the 65 ter Conference on the 14th of October, 2009, where you set out a number of alternatives, but we couldn't find a resolution anywhere of how this was to take place. It may be we've missed it but we don't think so. Of course it's important not only in respect of this witness, but in respect of the next, Christian Nielsen, where again only a small selection of the documents have been made to actually ask the witness about, but there are many others which are footnotes in his report but are also on our 65 ter list. So we are seeking the ruling or guidance from the Trial Chamber as to how we are going to have these documents admitted. The allied matter is the one that was dealt with yesterday in a written ruling. Now, Your Honours, this arose through, if I can call it, the Djeric mechanism of where you've got a large number of documents that the witness can deal with but a limited amount of time, how are these documents are to be dealt with. And we understood from Your Honours' ruling which is set out on the 26th of October that -- it's set out in the decision, the various steps that had to be taken. And I am afraid to say that I had assumed that we had taken those steps, and so I was somewhat surprised to have the application rejected on the basis that on the 4th of November, it was said that if -- in cases where we are dealing with a complex situation such as the introduction of a very large number of documents, we will then require a motion. It's fair to say that I had completely forgotten about that ruling in November, because it was in the middle of a long discussion again about the submission of documents. But in any event, Your Honours, it begs the question of what is a very large number of documents? And with Djeric it was 100, but with the witness with whom I was making this application it was nothing like that. And the motion is then being refused on the basis that we failed to file a motion and also that we failed to say how they relate to the indictment. Well, Your Honours, that may be our fault but we thought we had set out that they fall into the various categories of Serb Crisis Staff and whatever. What I'm actually coming to, and I think this is -- I can say this is really a position also taken by the Defence, is that we really would be most grateful for a time to be set aside to fully deal with and have a written direction in writing. It may be that we would like some further discussion in front of Your Honours as to how we are to deal with all the admission of these documents. I mean, that really is our position at the moment. But the urgency is, of course, how we now deal with the documents in Ms. Hanson's footnotes and Dr. Nielsen's footnotes, which are on our 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Does the Defence have any objection to the admission of further documents that are footnoted in the expert reports?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And which one, the 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: They are all on the 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yeah, the one which are on the 65 ter list, we don't have the objection. Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Let me think a minute because I always must to analyse position of OTP, you know, maybe something is around the bush, but at this stage, no, I don't have any objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: That's a wise man speaking, Mr. Pantelic, to think before you speak.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I hope you are not suggesting anything, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Certainly not. We are very well appraised of your good thinking, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I was put on note before that's why I gave my name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: In relation to the general aspect of admission of documents through 92 ter witnesses and expert witnesses, the Chamber agrees that it would be a good idea to have a discussion about this and to provide you with clear guide-lines. We thought that it was all clear but apparently it's not, so that in itself is a good reason to have a discussion about it. Maybe we should organise a 65 ter meeting for that purpose sometime early in the new year, or alternatively, the Chamber may just discuss it internally and then provide you with guide-lines. But in the interest of efficiency, it might be useful to sit down all together and discuss it before we adopt any final guide-lines.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think it would be of assistance if Your Honours perhaps were to issue - can we put it this way? - draft guide-lines and then we can make submissions on it. I think that's probably the most efficient way of dealing with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: That's exactly what we had in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That is definitely what we would prefer also and to have a 65 ter in the new year, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: In respect of the second issue relating to the additional documents to be admitted through Hanson and Nielsen, the Chamber's view was that this could cause prejudice to the Defence not having been put on notice that these extra documents would also be sought admitted into evidence. But since none of the Defence counsels have taken an issue with it, we agree. So they are all admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We rise until 2.15 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 10th day of December, 2009, at 2.15 p.m. 24 25
